dervis-irab:1-7.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَدُعُّ) means: he pushes away with violence and harshness. In al-Mukhtār: "daʿʿa, of the pattern of radda." Ibn Durayd said: daʿʿahu and daḥḥahu have one meaning; and a woman is daʿūʿ and daḥūḥ. He recited:
قبيح بالعجوز إذا تغدّت ... من البرنيّ واللبن الصريح
بتغّيها الرجال وفي صلاها ... مواقع كل فيشلة دحوح
(Ugly in an old woman, when she has had her midday meal of barnī dates and pure milk, / that she should seek men, while in her haunches are the places of every thrusting [member]; the text of the second verse is obscure.)
And Thaʿlab recited, on the authority of Ibn al-Aʿrābī:
قد أغتدي والليل في حريمه ... معسكرا في الغرّ من نجومه والصبح قد نسّم في أديمه ... يدعّه بضفّتي حيزومه
دعّ الربيب لحيتي يتيمه
(I set out at dawn while the night is still in its precinct, encamped among its bright stars, and the morning has breathed upon its surface, pushing it with the two sides of its chest, as the stepson shoves the beard of his orphan [stepchild].)
(الْماعُونَ) In al-Mukhtār: "al-māʿūn is a comprehensive name for the household's utilities, such as the pot and the axe and the like." The wording of Ibn Khālawayh is: "Al-māʿūn: obedience; al-māʿūn: zakāt; al-māʿūn: water; al-māʿūn: the ḥāl [? 'state']; al-māʿūn: the bucket, the fire-striker, the axe, fire, salt, and the like of what belongs to the dwellings. The dwellings were called māʿūn only because a traveller who has these things with him can settle wherever he wishes." Al-Rāʿī said:
قوم على الإسلام لما يمنعوا ... ماعونهم ويضيعوا التهليلا
(A people who, on Islam, had not yet withheld their māʿūn and had not yet neglected the declaration of tahlīl [lā ilāha illā llāh].)

* I'rab:
(أَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِي يُكَذِّبُ بِالدِّينِ) The hamza is for interrogation, and together with (رأيت) it means "tell me", as has often been stated before. It is also permissible that the seeing be of the heart, in which case it takes two objects, the first being the relative noun and the second omitted; the meaning is "Do you know who the one is who denies the Judgement?" It is also said that the seeing is of the eye, in which case there is no need to posit an object. (فَذلِكَ الَّذِي يَدُعُّ الْيَتِيمَ) The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa) because it introduces an apodosis of an implied condition, the implied form being "if you do not know him, then that is he." Al-Samīn put it as "if you seek knowledge of him, then that is he." (ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ and (الذي) is its khabar, and the clause (يدع اليتيم) is the ṣila (relative clause). It is strange that Ibn Khālawayh parsed (الذي) as an adjective of (ذلك) and did not mention the khabar at all, though he said that (ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ. There are other views and parsings mentioned by the exegetes; we have passed over them, as they are merely forced. (وَلا يَحُضُّ عَلى طَعامِ الْمِسْكِينِ) The wāw is a conjunction and (لا) is negative. (يحض) is an imperfect verb in the nominative and its fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he", i.e., the one who pushes the orphan away; (على طعام المسكين) are two elements attached to (يحض). (فَوَيْلٌ لِلْمُصَلِّينَ) The fāʾ is again the eloquent fāʾ, i.e., "if you have learned that he is characterised by these attributes, then woe", or "if the matter is so, then woe". This is preferable to al-Samīn's statement that it is the fāʾ of causation, which he explained by saying: "The fāʾ is of causation, i.e., the invocation of woe upon them is caused by these blameworthy attributes." (ويل) is a mubtadaʾ and (للمصلين) is its khabar. (الَّذِينَ هُمْ عَنْ صَلاتِهِمْ ساهُونَ) (الذين) is an adjective of (للمصلين); (هم) is a mubtadaʾ; (عن صلاتهم) is attached to (ساهون); and the nominal clause has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila of (الذين). We consider far-fetched the view of those who interpreted heedlessness "of" the prayer in the verse as heedlessness "in" the prayer, for heedlessness within it is neither a sin nor a reprehensible act for which the one who forgets is threatened with woe; every believer is liable to forget in his prayer, and this forgetfulness is made good by the prostration of forgetfulness (sujūd al-sahw) or by the sunnas and supererogatory prayers, as established in fiqh. (الَّذِينَ هُمْ يُراؤُنَ وَيَمْنَعُونَ الْماعُونَ) (الذين) is a badal (substitute) for the first (الذين); (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يراءون) is the khabar, and the clause is the ṣila of (الذين). The clause (يمنعون الماعون) is conjoined to (يراءون), falling within the scope of the ṣila. The first object of (يمنعون) is omitted, i.e., "people" or "those who ask", and (الماعون) is its second object.
